events.title: OG Coffee&Code Coding!
events.description:
C.O.D.E - Community of Developers & Engineers
# ☕ The OG CODE Meetup

### A Blockspace Community × CODE Collaboration

Before the hype. Before the buzzwords. Before “AI-powered everything.”
This is **The OG CODE**—the meetup that started it all, now presented in collaboration with the **Blockspace Community**.
No panels. No pitches. No pressure.
Just good people, good coffee, and focused time to build, learn, and connect.

## What this meetup is

An open, welcoming space for coders, builders, designers, and curious minds.
Bring your own project, homework, startup, side quest, experiment, or idea. Work at your own pace, meet other builders, ask questions, exchange ideas, or simply enjoy being productive around like-minded people.
Expect:

* Focused building time
* Organic conversations
* Spontaneous debugging
* Knowledge sharing
* Genuine community

This meetup is beginner-friendly, expert-respected, and ego-free.

## What this meetup is not

❌ A lecture
❌ A sales event
❌ A recruiting trap
❌ A 90-minute presentation

## How it works

1. Show up
2. Grab coffee ☕
3. Open your laptop, notebook, or sketchpad
4. Work at your own pace
5. Chat when you want and focus when you need
6. Leave having made progress—or at least a new friend

## Who should attend

* Software engineers and data professionals
* Students and self-learners
* Founders and indie hackers
* Designers, tinkerers, and technologists
* Members of the Blockspace and CODE communities
* Anyone who enjoys building things with other humans

Whether this is your first CODE, you are part of the Blockspace Community, or you have been attending since day one, you are welcome.
This collaboration brings together two communities around a shared goal: creating a relaxed, supportive space where people can build, learn, and connect.

**Come for the code.**
**Stay for the community.**
**Leave caffeinated. ☕🚀**

events.title: DataPhilly Webinar series: Confidence Intervals: How Much Can We Trust a Number?
events.description:
C.O.D.E - Community of Developers & Engineers
📢 Join DataPhilly for an online session with Raymond McCollum, who explains confidence intervals in an easy-to-follow way. The talk starts with simple averages, moves through regression, and ends with modern machine-learning models such as XGBoost.
**What you’ll learn:**

* Why more data usually improves confidence
* Why some parts of the data carry more information than others
* How to measure uncertainty in complex predictions

**Speaker Bio:**
Raymond A. McCollum, Ph.D., is a data scientist and statistician with over 25 years of experience spanning defense, aerospace, and financial industries. His work includes applying statistics and data science to anti-submarine warfare for the U.S. Navy, conducting uncertainty analysis in heat shield measurements for NASA’s Mars Lander, and developing automated underwriting systems for Prudential Financial. Over his career—from entry-level analyst to Vice President of Data Science—he has been recognized for innovative problem-solving and creative analytic design. He discovered that the mathematics underlying data analysis remains consistent across disciplines, forming the foundation for both classical statistics and modern data science. As Founder and CEO of Statistical Data Science Solutions (StatDSS), he focuses on advancing statistical rigor in real-world data science applications.
🔗 Webinar access: [https://meet.google.com/aki-vdjp-ibg](https://meet.google.com/aki-vdjp-ibg)

# C.O.D.E. @ Pennovation Works — Innovation Hub Build Day

Join **C.O.D.E Community of Developers & Engineers** at Pennovation Works on **Nov 13** for an open build day focused on making progress, sharing ideas, and collaborating with other builders across Philadelphia.
Pennovation Works is the University of Pennsylvania’s innovation campus, bringing together startups, researchers, engineers, founders, and teams working on new technology and products.
This is a working session rather than a formal presentation. Bring whatever you are currently building and spend the day alongside other developers, founders, designers, researchers, and technical creatives.
You can:

* Work on your own project
* Pair program or collaborate with others
* Get feedback on something you’re building
* Meet potential collaborators
* Work through technical blockers
* Prototype a new idea
* Contribute to an open-source project
* Simply bring your laptop and get some focused work done

There is no required project, stack, company, or experience level. Whether you are building an AI agent, startup, open-source tool, research project, side project, or just experimenting with something new, you are welcome to join.
**Date:** **Nov 13**
**Location:** Pennovation Works, Philadelphia
Bring your laptop, something you want to work on, and a willingness to build with other people.
Hosted by **C.O.D.E Community of Developers & Engineers**.

events.description:
C.O.D.E - Community of Developers & Engineers
```
Join Eric Manganaro and Justin DiClemente at Pennovation Center for Reverse Engineer Anything (REA), with two talks on Rust and CNC control.

Eric Manganaro: Building a library of ideas with Rust
Eric will show how he uses Rust to capture ideas from programs he reverse engineers. His REA system stores recurring themes and architectural patterns so he can reuse them in new projects, in Rust or other languages.

Justin DiClemente: REA for industrial automation
Justin will show how REA applies to CNC control. A planned demo will run actual controller firmware against a simulated FPGA and a virtual CNC mill, tracing software commands through to machine motion.

Time permitting, we’ll also look at proprietary 3D printer software, with Bambu Lab as a possible example.

Pennovation Center
3401 Grays Ferry Avenue, Philadelphia, PA
```

events.title: Online Talk and Demo : The Context Layer for a Grounded Data Agent
events.description:
C.O.D.E - Community of Developers & Engineers
**Abstract**
Data agents are most useful when they understand the data they work with, not only its structure. This talk explores how a context layer helps an agent make better decisions and write accurate SQL that stays grounded in the business. We will look at the building blocks of context, including ontology and a context graph, and how they come together so an agent can retrieve what is relevant, reason over it, check its own work and respond with confidence. We will also cover how to measure the incremental changes with evaluations. Attendees will leave with a clear mental model and practical patterns for building context-aware data agents.
A 10-minute live demo of a simple Data Agent using Langchain’s Deep Agent, follows the talk.
**Details**

* **Format:** 60 minutes: a 35 to 40 minute talk, a 10-minute live demo and 10 minutes for Q&A.
* **Audience:** data, analytics and AI engineers building agents on top of databases.
* **Level:** Intermediate.

**Bio**
Saket is a Principal Data Engineer

He specializes in building modern and highly scalable data platforms. This also includes driving Data platform AI strategy and Governance.

**Date & Time**
Nov 13th 8:30 pm EST

events.title: Claude Code vs. Codex: Loops, Graphs, and Harnesses
events.description:
C.O.D.E - Community of Developers & Engineers
## Claude Code vs. Codex: Loops, Graphs, and Harnesses

This is a casual pair-programming meetup for developers experimenting with Claude Code, Codex, and agentic coding workflows.
There is no formal presentation and no fixed curriculum. Bring a laptop, a repository, a side project, or a workflow you want to test. We will work in small groups, compare approaches, debug problems, and share what is working.

Possible areas to explore include:

* Building iterative coding-agent loops
* Comparing Claude Code and Codex on the same task
* Designing graph-based agent workflows
* Creating reusable coding harnesses
* Managing context across large repositories
* Running tests and validating agent-generated changes
* Using sandboxes, permissions, and approval steps
* Coordinating subagents or parallel tasks
* Measuring latency, token usage, cost, and completion quality
* Debugging failed or incomplete agent runs

You do not need to be an expert in either tool. This meetup is for people who want hands-on time to experiment, pair with other developers, and learn through building.
Bring something you are working on, or join someone else’s project.
Hosted by **Coffee & Code Philadelphia**.
